title: Architectural design
tagline: {agent_The} is a controlled agent runtime, not just an LLM with tools: the LLM proposes, the platform controls.

stop_rules.head: Research stops at the first rule that fires; the limits are checked before the others.

by_rule.sufficient_evidence: Enough evidence: every question that needs outside research has an answer backed by a ledger source.
by_rule.no_marginal_gain: Nothing new: the last {no_marginal_gain_window} iterations added no new source.
by_rule.deadline: Deadline: {report_reserve_s} s before the run's deadline, so verify and report still fit.

stop_rules.foot: Research also ends after {max_research_iterations} iterations at most.

invariants.head: The checks code runs on the review before report.json is written:

by_invariant.03: INV-03 Schema: the review matches the spec, with unique finding IDs and ranks.
by_invariant.04: INV-04 Anchors: every quoted anchor resolves in the canonical text.
by_invariant.05: INV-05 Citations: every cited evidence ID is in the ledger, and every URL in the report is allowed.
by_invariant.06: INV-06 Recommendations: each has an issue, rationale, benefit, change and supporting evidence.
by_invariant.07: INV-07 Degradations: every degradation is disclosed by a limitation, and every limitation cites one.
by_invariant.08: INV-08 Secrets: no canary secret appears in any file of the run.
by_invariant.09: INV-09 Manifest: the run manifest is complete: git SHA, hashes, models and tools.
by_invariant.10: INV-10 Registry: the decision registry hash never changes, and every cited decision exists.
by_invariant.12: INV-12 Finding IDs: every finding ID the review cites is one of its findings.
by_invariant.13: INV-13 Re-assessment: in a re-assessment, every previous finding has exactly one status.

important.title: Why not LangGraph
important.lead: A **custom state machine** was chosen so that the __orchestration logic stays visible and controllable__, above all around __budgets__, __stop rules__, __evidence__ and __robustness__.

points.text: This project needed very specific behaviour around:

points: **LangGraph** came closest, at {score_langgraph} of 100 against {score_custom} for the custom loop. Its checkpointing and replay are built in, but its MCP adapter is __pinned to MCP 1.x__, tool transport failures __need wrapper code__, and its channels, reducers and ToolNode __take a walkthrough of their own__.

points.text: **The other frameworks**, scored on the same weighted matrix:
sub: **PydanticAI**, {score_pydanticai}: the best for swapping vendors, but it __hides the loop__ inside Agent.run and adds retries of its own.
**OpenAI Agents SDK**, {score_openai_agents}: good retry primitives, but __still 0.x__, with a default tool timeout too short for a cold MCP server.
**LangChain create_agent**, {score_langchain}: __all of LangGraph's dependencies__ without its explicit control flow.
**Claude Agent SDK**, {score_claude_agent_sdk}: a __bundled CLI__ with its own system prompt, tools and compaction, the hardest to explain.
**CrewAI**, {score_crewai}: a __dependency conflict__ with the current Anthropic SDK, and many hidden prompts.
**smolagents**, {score_smolagents}: __MCP broken on 2.x__, and it executes model-written code.

points: [See the weighted decision matrix](https://github.com/malcolm1232/SIT/tree/claude/eloquent-sagan-ah5ttk/research/frameworks#weighted-decision-matrix)

important.title: Two choke points
important.lead: The single most important architectural idea in the repo: __everything external goes through two choke points__, the **LLMGateway** and the **ToolGateway**.
points: A phase never touches an SDK or a server, so __a backend can be replaced__ behind the same interface: Codex or OpenAI would be __one more LLMGateway class__. None is built yet, and it is not free, because the tool schemas and structured outputs are Anthropic-shaped.

important.title: Choke point 2: the ToolGateway
important.lead: Every tool call passes through __the same layers, outermost first__:
points: **PolicyToolGateway** checks every call: the __allowed server__, the __allowed tool__, the URL policy, the argument sanitiser, the server's circuit breaker and the tool-call budget.
Because every call runs through this choke point, __any call can be denied__: a refused call comes back as blocked and never reaches the server.

important.foot: A generic agentic framework __would hide some of those decisions__.

important.title: The evidence ledger
important.lead: Instead of letting the model write __"According to https://somewebsite.com..."__, the agent __creates an evidence record__ for every source: **EV-(n)**.

diagram.sub: a search result or a fetched page

points: The model then __references EV-002__ rather than inventing a URL.
This gives **provenance**: don't trust the generated answer; __establish a chain back to the source__.

simple.lead: The user gives {agent_the} one technical design document and gets back a review of it.
points: Every finding is anchored to a quoted passage of that document.
A change is recommended only when {agent_the} can say what is wrong, why, what evidence supports it and what the change would gain; otherwise it says no change, with a reason.
An earlier version can be given too, and the run becomes a re-assessment against it.

items: A PDF, or a page-marked .txt or Markdown file.
Optionally an earlier version (--v1) or the run directory of a prior review (--previous); every prior finding then gets exactly one status in the delta table.
Each recommendation names the problem, the reason, the evidence and the gain, or the finding carries a no-change rationale instead.

simple.lead: The CLI is the interface: one command, dra review <pdf>, runs the whole review.
points: This page starts the same command as a subprocess, so the page adds nothing to the agent.
Other commands work on a run directory: resume, replay, explain, coverage and states.
Flags change a run without touching code: --profile demo, --no-tools, --deadline, --faults.

items: run (alias review), resume, replay, explain, coverage, states, preflight, selftest and ui.
sit-review and dra are the same entry point.
0 ok, 2 usage, 3 LLM unavailable, 4 stage crash, 5 resume drift, 130 interrupted.
A run that degrades but discloses it still writes its report and exits 0 with outcome completed_degraded.
Start review runs dra review as a subprocess; the run directory stays the only state.

simple.lead: Ingest is code, not a model: pdfplumber turns the PDF into one page-marked canonical text, and every later quote is checked against those same bytes.
points: It produces a Document: pages, sections and an index of the requirement IDs the text mentions.
The canonical text is stored once and hashed, and both the model and the verifier read it.
On the {backend_default} backend the model reads this text only; on the Anthropic API backend the native PDF block goes alongside it, for tables, images and layout.

contrast.bad: The model reads the PDF its own way, and the verifier reads a different extraction: a quote can look right to one and wrong to the other.
contrast.better: One canonical text, one extractor, read by the model and the verifier alike: deterministic quote matching.

items: Reads the input file (PDF through pdfplumber, else text).
Writes the page-marked text with [[PAGE n]] markers and a section index under text/, and each document's hashes, page count and whether a native PDF block is used into the run state.
ADR-006: the model gets both views and is told to quote only from the canonical text.
The Claude Code backend sets native_pdf to false, so on it the canonical text carries the document.
advanced.src: docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-006; agent/sit_review_agent/llm/claude_code.py native_pdf; agent/sit_review_agent/llm/prefix.py document_prefix_message

simple.lead: The orchestrator is the coordinator: it sets up the runtime, then drives the stages in order and decides what runs at the same time.
points: Before any model call it checks the MCP key, creates the run directory, builds the gateways, attaches the run limits to the LLM stack, starts the MCP warm-up, runs the LLM preflight and loads any fault schedule.
During the run it starts stage 1's members as concurrent tasks, checks the caps before stage 1 and refine, and writes a checkpoint after every ended phase.
When a run fails it maps the error to an exit code and writes failure.json, which says why and how to resume.

items: run_review: tool key check, run directory, effective config, LLM and tool gateways, background MCP warm-up right after the tool stack exists, LLM preflight, initial manifest, run limits attached.
Orchestrator.run walks the stages; stage 1 runs its members as asyncio tasks on one event loop, with no threads.
A member still running {stage1_grace_s} s after the stage 1 limit is stopped and disclosed; its code fallback stands.
A cap that fires before stage 1 or refine skips the run to verify, so a report is still written.
Errors are typed and mapped to exit codes; failure.json records the phase, the completed phases and whether the run is resumable.

simple.lead: At the highest level, {agent_the} is an explicit state-machine orchestrator: each phase has a defined responsibility, and the orchestrator controls transitions, budgets, deadlines and checkpoints.
points: The state machine answers: what stage are we in, and what may run next? The orchestrator answers: given that, what do I execute and how do I coordinate it?
A run is {stage_count} stages in a fixed order: {stage_order}.
Stage 1 holds {stage_1_members}; research waits for {research_waits_for}, the others start together.
The path only goes forward. Its one shortcut is also forward: a cap that fires before stage 1 or refine sends the run to verify, so a report is still written.

contrast.bad: The LLM controls the whole workflow: what to do next and when to stop.
contrast.better: An explicit state machine owns the transitions, and the model works inside one phase at a time.

items: PhaseName (eight phases), STAGE_ORDER, STAGE_MEMBERS, STAGE_TRANSITIONS (linear), STAGE_ON_CAP (stage 1 and refine jump to verify), STAGE_1_DEPENDS.
A stage 1 member ends done, cut (running when the limit fired, keeps what it salvaged) or skipped (never started).
Only research and refine may be disabled in config/agent.yaml.
advanced.src: agent/sit_review_agent/states.py STAGE_1_DEPENDS; agent/sit_review_agent/states.py OPTIONAL_PHASES; config/agent.yaml phases

items: dra states prints the graph as Mermaid from the same tables, so the diagram cannot drift.

ADR-001: a custom loop on the Anthropic SDK with a direct MCP client, chosen on a weighted matrix (custom 92, LangGraph 80, PydanticAI 77), so every retry, degradation and log line is code that can be shown and tested.
A LangGraph variant of the same agent was built and compared; the custom loop was kept.

simple.lead: Understand builds a structured understanding of the document for the phases after it, and that becomes part of the run state.
points: The **intent summary**: __what__ the __design is for__, its __objectives__, __constraints__ and __key assumptions__.
The **decision registry**: the __approved decisions__, __pending decisions__, __constraints__ and __requirements__ the __document states__, numbered AD-(n).
The registry is then frozen and hashed.
The **__important thing__** is that UNDERSTAND **__produces structured state__**, rather than just returning a paragraph.

contrast.bad: UNDERSTAND: "Here's what I think this document means..." Then RESEARCH: "Let me figure out what that paragraph means..."
contrast.better: UNDERSTAND -> structured output -> STATE -> RESEARCH and REFINE.

items: UnderstandOutput: intent_summary (statement, objectives, constraints, key_assumptions, doc_anchors), registry (type, doc_ref, statement, doc_anchor), document_version, review_inputs_found.
Registry types: approved_decision, pending_decision, constraint, requirement.
It starts with plan and the assess shards, so neither sees it; research and refine read the intent and the frozen registry.
A finding that would reverse an approved decision must declare it as a challenge with at least two evidence items (INV-10).
The review has no intent summary or registry from the model, and the cut is disclosed.

simple.lead: Plan converts the review criteria into concrete research questions, decides which need external research, and which research capability should be used.

points.text: **Job 1**: turn each of the **{criteria_count} criteria** (provided by {agent_the}) into __questions__, usually one to three.
sub: Eg. a criterion: Does the design handle failure and recovery appropriately?
RQ-001: How does the payment service recover after a downstream timeout?
RQ-002: Does the retry strategy risk duplicate transactions?

points: **Job 2**: decide whether a **question** __needs external research__; consistency, completeness and verifiability are answered from the document.
**Job 3**: decide WHICH research capability to use.
**Job 4**: give Research search queries.
**Job 5**: budget the research.

items: PlanOutput: questions (id RQ-nnn, criterion_id, question, rationale, needs_external, capability, queries, section_refs) and criteria_skipped (criterion_id, reason).
build_plan drops questions for unknown criteria, sets capability none when its server is disabled, and adds a document-only question for every criterion the model neither asked about nor skipped.
The plan sets no budget per question: research as a whole may make at most {max_tool_calls} tool calls in {max_research_iterations} iterations.
--plan-only stops after the plan with zero tool calls; plan_approval: true waits for approval before research.

simple.lead: Instead of one huge assess call, the criteria are divided into {shard_count} groups, or shards, that run side by side.
points: **Each shard** __receives the document__ and its __own criteria__, works against an __isolated copy__ of the __run state__, and __produces draft findings__.
Those are **concurrent phase executions**, not {shard_count} independent agents: asyncio tasks in one process, each waiting on its own model call.
**Each finished shard** is __stored__ as a __serialisable result__, so resume re-runs only the shards that had not finished.
It's not merely "let's run {shard_count} LLMs". It's "let's __parallelize independent work__ while __preserving deterministic state ownership__ and making each shard resumable."

contrast.bad: **One huge assess** call over every criterion: the slowest step of the run, and __one failure costs__ the __whole assessment__.
contrast.better: **{shard_count} shards side by side**: the __stage takes as long as its slowest shard__, and a __failed shard costs__ only its __own criteria__.

items: Each criterion is in exactly one group. A criterion added live that is in no group becomes its own shard, so it adds a parallel call, not wall time.
One conversation, assess-0-s<k>, answering AssessOutput: findings, sound_areas, coverage (every criterion: findings, no_issue or not_applicable).
Reads the document, its criteria and the review mode; no intent, registry, plan answers or evidence register.
Each stage 1 member works on a deep copy of the run state and is merged back when it ends, so a checkpoint never holds half-written state.
A shard's result is a StateDelta, stored in shards/<k>-<name>.json.
A shard that hangs, refuses, is truncated or crashes leaves the other shards' findings intact, and its own criteria are marked not assessed.
ADR-011: the sequential design with one assess call could not fit the demo slot; the criteria were split into shards that run side by side (four at first, six since USER_DECISIONS #40).

simple.lead: Research is the agentic loop: reason → act → observe → then reason again.
points: It runs **after understand and plan**: it __starts once__ both have __ended__, beside the assess shards.
It **works** on the **plan's external questions**. The model __chooses the tool calls__; the __platform runs them__ and __records__ every result as **__evidence__** before the model sees it.
It is built from the **LLMGateway** when it __needs to reason__, the **ToolGateway** when it __needs the outside world__, and the __run state__.
Its evidence meets the findings in refine, after the shards are merged.
simple.flow: "LLM, what should I investigate?" → LLMGateway → Claude → "Search for X" → ToolGateway → MCP → search result → back to state → LLM again

items: At most {max_research_iterations} iterations, {max_rounds_per_iteration} tool rounds per iteration and {max_tool_calls} tool calls; tool text shown to the model is capped at {max_tool_text_chars} characters, the full payload stays in tools.jsonl.
Active stop rules: {active_stop_rules}.
The model may vote to stop; code honours the vote only when no external question is still open and at least one tool call was made.
An answered question needs {min_independent_sources} independent sources or one primary official source, else it is partial.
ResearchOutput: answers (question_id, status answered, partial, unanswered or conflicting, summary, evidence_ids), stop_requested, stop_rationale.
No tools or every server down: a tool_unavailable degradation, open external questions become unanswered, the run continues document-only.
A refusal is retried once with review framing; a call cut by the deadline ends research with stop reason deadline.
ADR-001: the tool loop is our own code, not the SDK's tool runner, so every round, stop and degradation can be logged and tested.

simple.lead: Reason is the model's turn: what to investigate, which tool, which search query, what next.
points: **"LLM, what should I investigate?"** goes through the **LLMGateway to Claude**, which answers "search for X".
The **model reads** the __open external questions__ with the __plan's suggested queries__, the __registry__ and __decides what is still missing__.
The **backend is swappable**: {backend_list_marked}, default {backend_default}.

items: Tools are offered by capability under the name <server>__<tool>, from whatever each enabled server lists, so no tool name is hard-coded.
One research conversation per run, with the shared document prefix and the research brief; the next round, the wrap-up and the repair turns are parts of the same prompt file.

simple.lead: **ACT** is the **platform's turn**: __every tool call__ the __model asked for__ runs through the __ToolGateway, never straight from the model to a server__.
points: The **calls** of one round __run concurrently__, and every result goes back in one message, failures marked as errors.
**Policy checks** each call before it leaves the process.
The **live servers** are __MCP over streamable HTTP__: {servers_enabled} are enabled.

items: Results return in the order of the model's tool calls; nothing is dropped, and a call over the budget gets a "not executed" error result.

A session the server closed is reopened once and the call retried once; a session idle for more than {session_idle_reopen_s} s is reopened before the next call; a tool is disabled for the run only after {tool_error_limit} genuine failures in a row.
advanced.src: agent/sit_review_agent/tools/gateway.py MCPToolGateway; agent/sit_review_agent/tools/gateway.py TOOL_ERROR_LIMIT; config/tools.yaml session_idle_reopen_s

simple.lead: **Observe** __turns__ each __result into evidence__ the platform owns: __sources become **EV-(n) ledger**__ entries.
points: So the __model__ can **cite only** what it has read, in **Evidence Ledger** by ID.
**Question statuses**, __tool calls__ and the budget counters __go into__ the **run state**.
**The [stop rules](tip:stop_rules)** are __checked after every tool round__ and __every iteration__; then the __model reasons again__, or the __loop ends__.
Repeat until done, or until a limit is hit.

items: Each result is parsed into sources; each source gets an authority class and an independence key; a URL already in the ledger is reused, so only new sources count as progress.
Question statuses and evidence on the plan, tool_calls, queries_issued, new sources per iteration, unanswered_questions, stop_reason, and the registry hash per iteration.

simple.lead: Merge: when stage 1 closes, the **shards' findings** become __one list__ in the __run state.__
points: **Findings** are r__enumbered FND-(n)__ in __shard order__.
The list is **ranked** by __severity__, then __confidence__.
The **shards**' __document__ and __inference evidence goes into__ the __ledger__.
A **map** from **each shard's own IDs** to the merged IDs is kept, so __every finding__ can be __traced back to its shard.__

items: AssessPhase.merge renumbers and ranks; Orchestrator._close merges in shard order and writes the stage's closing checkpoint.
A shard with no result at the close is recorded as cut and its criteria are not assessed.
finding_drafts, finding_meta, finding_ids.shards, sound_area_drafts, coverage, and the shards' ledger entries.

simple.lead: **Refine** is __one model call__ over __every merged finding__: it sees all the shards' findings together with the registry, the **research answers** and the __ledger__, and __returns one revision per finding__.
points: **Keep**: with the __final rank__, __severity__ and disposition, the registry links, and any research evidence to add.
**Merge**: fold a __duplicate into a kept finding__, typically the same issue found by two shards.
**Withdraw**: __unsupported__ evidence.
This is where **research evidence** __meets__ the __findings__.

contrast.bad: Ask the model to __write every finding out again.__
contrast.better: Ask for **one revision per finding**, a __patch__ that code applies __exactly__.

items: RefineRevisionsOutput: revisions (finding_id, action keep, merge or withdraw, merge_into, rank, severity, disposition, affected_decisions, added_evidence, next_step, reason).
Code checks one revision per finding, the action rules, ranks 1..n and no evidence added twice; every revision that holds on its own is kept, and at most one repair call asks for the failing ones.
Refine is optional. If it is off, cut or fails, the merged findings ordered by severity stand, disclosed. On the demo profile it must end by {demo_refine_end} s.

simple.lead: **Verify** is where the **platform**, __not the model__, __checks code__ against every quoted anchor __against the canonical text.__
points: The **quote is searched** for __verbatim first__, __then fuzzily__ at {fuzzy_threshold} or better, near the cited page and section.
A **finding with no anchor** that resolves is __moved__ to the __unresolved list as Unverified__, with __no recommendation__, and the report says so.
Evidence is hydrated from the ledger: the model never writes a URL, and a URL that is not in the ledger is removed.
One repair call may re-quote the failing anchors, only when more than {repair_min_slack_s} s remain. It never sends the run back to research: the next stage is report.

items: An anchor is a verbatim quote of at least {min_quote_tokens} tokens with a page and section; search within the cited page plus or minus one, narrowed to the cited section plus or minus one when it resolves.
Every anchor is recorded in anchors.json as resolved, repaired or unresolved.
Unknown evidence IDs, URLs in free text not in the ledger, registry conflicts, hollow fields, verdict against severities.
Conversation verify, answer AnchorRepairOutput; skipped and disclosed when {repair_min_slack_s} s or less remain before the verify and verdict reserve.
Verification is code against the canonical text and the ledger; a second-model judge is in the harness, where it can be blinded.

simple.lead: **Report** is __one model__ call that __returns only the verdict__; code assembles the rest of the review.
points: The model may **say fit**, **fit with conditions** or **not fit**; only code can say not assessed, with the reason.
[**Code runs** __{invariant_count} invariant checks__](tip:invariants) before __report.json is written__: __anchors resolve__, __citations__ are in the ledger, degradations are disclosed.
The **limitations** are __written by code__ from the degradations, never by the model.
**report.md** is __rendered__ from __report.json__ with a template, so the file and this page cannot disagree.

items: VerdictOutput from the model; not_assessed is set by code only, with the reason deadline, truncated or declined.
On the demo profile the verdict call must end by {demo_verdict_end} s, else a rule-based verdict stands.
advanced.src: agent/sit_review_agent/llm/outputs.py VerdictOutput; agent/sit_review_agent/phases/report.py not_assessed_verdict; config/profiles/demo.yaml verdict_end

items: assemble_review builds the review, settles finding IDs across every renumbering, runs check_all, renders the Markdown and finalises the manifest.

simple.lead: A **run directory holds everything** about the run: the __review__, the __evidence__, and every log needed to explain or replay it.
points: **report.md** and **report.json**: the __verified findings__ and __the verdict.__
ledger.json: the evidence ledger. anchors.json: every quote and how it resolved.
manifest.json, checkpoints/, shards/, the call logs and progress.log.

items: manifest.json, effective_config.json, report.json, report.md, ledger.jsonl and ledger.json, anchors.json, state.json, checkpoints/, shards/, llm.jsonl, tools.jsonl, text/, progress.log and progress.jsonl, failure.json when a run fails.
Written before the first model call with outcome crashed, finalised at exit with models, usage, cost, timings and output hashes, so a run that dies never reads as completed.
dra explain <finding-id> reads only the run directory: anchors with match scores, evidence with the tool call behind it, and the finding's history across phases.

simple.lead: Every model phase calls the model through one protocol, the LLMGateway; phases never touch an SDK.
points: Live backends: the Claude Code CLI run headless, the default, which bills the Claude subscription with no API key; and the Anthropic API, behind the same protocol.
Replay serves recorded calls, Fake serves scripted answers for tests, and a fault-injecting wrapper sits under the retries for robustness tests.
The gateway owns retries, typed stop reasons, one effort level per conversation, and the call log.

contrast.bad: Each phase calls a provider SDK directly.
contrast.better: One swappable backend: another provider would be one more LLMGateway.

items: ClaudeCodeGateway and AnthropicGateway (llm.backend: {backend_list}, default {backend_default}); ReplayLLMGateway for dra replay; FakeGateway for transport fake; FaultInjectingLLMGateway when a fault schedule is set.
Transports: {transports}.

advanced.h: Why the CLI is the default
items: ADR-010: the owner's calls bill the subscription or cloud credits rather than a separate API key; the API backend stays for evaluators who hold a key.

Retries with backoff, one refusal retry with review framing, a pre-send size check against {context_margin_pct} % of the context window, a first-call network window of {first_call_window_s} s so an offline start fails fast, output capped at {max_tokens} tokens, model {model}.
Each attempt's timeout is the time left before its stage ends.

simple.lead: Every tool call goes through one protocol, the ToolGateway, built as layers wrapped around the real MCP client.
points: Outermost first: logging, policy, self-replay on resume, fault injection, recording, then the base: the live MCP client, a cassette replay or a fake.
Fault injection sits below the policy, so a test proves the policy handles the fault rather than the injector hiding it.
{server_count} MCP servers are configured; {servers_enabled} are enabled.

items: {tool_layer_chain}.
{servers_disabled} are off: browser automation keeps one shared browser for every caller with no domain allowlist, and document intelligence rejected its only probed sample.
One long-lived session per server; {connect_timeout_s} s allowed for a cold first connect; a background warm-up overlaps ingest and understand.
The key is read from SIT_MCP_API_KEY and never logged; a missing key fails the run before any model call unless --no-tools asks for a document-only review.

simple.lead: Policy decides whether a tool call may leave the process: allowed, it continues; not allowed, it is rejected.
points: Only allowlisted tools of enabled servers.
A fetched URL must have appeared in an earlier result or in the document.
No secret, key-shaped token or bulk document text may leave in a tool argument.
A per-server breaker and the tool-call budget are enforced here too.

items: The allowlist, the URL policy (a query string added to a seen URL is refused), the argument sanitiser, the per-server breaker (a tool disabled after {tool_error_limit} genuine failures in a row), the budget.
advanced.src: agent/sit_review_agent/tools/policy.py check_urls; agent/sit_review_agent/tools/policy.py sanitise_args; agent/sit_review_agent/tools/gateway.py PolicyToolGateway; config/url_policy.yaml

simple.lead: The runtime **maintains structured** state that is __read__ and __updated__ by the phases, the LLM gateway and the tool execution flow.
points: It **holds the documents**, the __intent summary__ and the __registry__, the __plan__, the __tool calls__, __draft__, __verified findings__, the __unresolved__, the __stop reason__ and the __budget__ (tool calls, tokens, iterations and time; see Advanced).
The **evidence ledger** is kept beside it as its own __append-only__ journal.
**Stage 1** members __each work on a copy of it__ and are __merged back when they end__.
So the **LLM** is only one __subsystem__: the **platform owns what state** the __run is in__.

items: documents, intent_summary, registry, registry_frozen, registry_hashes, plan, tool_calls, queries_issued, finding_drafts, finding_ids, coverage, findings, sound_areas, anchor_table, verdict, unresolved, limitations, degradations, stop_reason, budget.
Written to state.json, and snapshotted into every checkpoint.
isolate gives a member its own deep copy; merge_member copies back what it replaced and appends what it added.

simple.lead: Evidence is not just dumped into the prompt: the platform owns it in a ledger, and the model cites it by ID, like EV-002.
points: [See Advanced: Merge: the shards' findings in one list](run:merge)

rows: A source from a __successful tool call__ of this run; carries that call's ID.
A __quoted passage__ of the design document.
A conclusion __drawn from other entries__, which it names.

contrast.bad: The model says: "I found this website..."
contrast.better: The platform recorded the source, and the model cites EV-002.

items: External (from a tool call), doc (canonical text by page and section) and inference (lists what it is derived from, every ID already in the ledger).
Appended to ledger.jsonl, flushed per entry; ledger.json is the snapshot the report writes.
INV-05 fails the review on a cited evidence ID that is not in the ledger; a model-written URL found in neither the ledger nor the document is removed and disclosed.

simple.lead: After every phase the orchestrator writes a checkpoint, so a stopped run resumes where it stopped and a finished run can be replayed exactly.
points: Each checkpoint pins the hashes of the config, the prompt bundle and the canonical text.
dra resume refuses if those hashes drifted, and re-runs only the members and shards that had not finished.
A tool call that succeeded before the stop is served from tools.jsonl, never made again.
dra replay runs the real phases again with the recorded model and tool calls; a request that does not match its recording stops the replay.

items: Atomic; pins effective_config, prompts_bundle and canonical_text hashes and the byte offsets of the three journals; in stage 1 every member writes its own when it ends.
Loads the latest checkpoint, refuses on drift unless --accept-drift, truncates the ledger to the checkpoint offset, restores the run clock.
Model calls served by conversation and request hash, tool calls from tools.jsonl, time from a virtual clock; the replayed report is stamped replayed evidence.

simple.lead: Budgets are the platform's limits, enforced by code: a deadline, stage limits on the run clock, and caps on research.
points: The demo profile ends stage 1 by {demo_stage_1_end} s, refine by {demo_refine_end} s and the verdict call by {demo_verdict_end} s, inside a {demo_deadline_s} s deadline.
Each model call is bounded by the time left before its stage ends, so one slow call cannot take the report with it.
Research stops at {max_tool_calls} tool calls or {max_research_iterations} iterations, or earlier when the evidence is sufficient or new sources dry up.
A limit that cuts a phase keeps what it salvaged, and the cut is disclosed.

items: Active: {active_stop_rules}; each is a registered function returning a closed stop-reason code.
Absolute seconds on the run clock, not a fraction of the deadline, because the thinking time of a call is a fixed cost. The base profile's deadline is {deadline_s} s.

items: Every degraded path is a numbered DEG-nnn with its event and impact, and the report has one limitation per degradation (INV-07).

simple.lead: Fault injection lets {agent_the} show it fails honestly: a schedule makes a tool hang, a model refuse or truncate, the network drop or a phase crash, on purpose.
points: The same schedule file drives a test and a live run, with --faults.
The injectors sit below the policy and retry layers, so the test exercises the real handling.
The oracles are the run invariants: a valid review, every anchor resolving, every citation in the ledger, every degradation disclosed, no secret in any file.

items: FaultInjectingGateway for tools, FaultInjectingLLMGateway for the model, and a process fault wrapper for phases and shards.

simple.lead: The repository separates the agent from the evaluation harness: harness/ is never imported by the agent, and a test proves it.
points: The evaluation items are synthetic design documents with planted flaws and a sealed answer key.
sit-eval score matches a review against its key; sit-eval grade is a key-blind grader on the lab's rubric.
The analysis is pre-registered, and a score on an answer key the owner has not signed off is marked exploratory.

contrast.bad: The agent grades its own review.
contrast.better: A separate, blinded harness that the agent never imports.

items: A test walks the agent package's syntax tree and fails on any import of the harness.
A judge scores candidate pairs 0 to 3, a Hungarian assignment picks the one-to-one matching, unmatched findings are adjudicated, and grounding judges check citation support.
Hypotheses, metrics and decision rules in one file, with a deviations log.

simple.lead: {agent_The} is a controlled agent runtime, not just an LLM with tools: the LLM proposes, and the platform controls state, policy, tools, evidence, checkpoints, verification and budgets.
points: The platform controls what state the run is in, what the model can see, which tools it may call, what evidence is recorded, what can be replayed, which failures can be injected, which checkpoints exist, when the workflow moves on, and when verification passes.

"I built an agent runtime where the LLM is not allowed to directly control the entire application. The platform owns the lifecycle, state transitions, tool access, checkpoints, reproducibility and evaluation."

items: State machine: states.py. Policy: tools/policy.py. Evidence: state/evidence_ledger.py. Checkpoints: state/checkpoint.py. Verification: phases/verify.py and invariants.py. Budgets: stop_rules.py and llm/runtime.py.
